text:
marta: Heads-up: p99 jumped ~15% on nightly for the attention kernel-selection change after yesterday's selector refactor. Observed on the 1k-seqbench run. tagging @aj @liam @perf-bot
perf-bot: Nightly summary (job=nightly/attn-select, id=nb-2024-06-07-03): baseline commit: a1b2c3 -> new commit: d4e5f6
  - throughput: -2%
  - p50: +1ms
  - p95: +8ms
  - p99: +42ms
  - sample N=1200 requests
aj: Oof. Can you paste the exact bench command + selector flags used? Need to know sampling window and kernel ordering.
marta: Sure. Ran from the selector branch: kernel-selector/refactor/d4e5f6. Command:
```
./bench/run_bench.sh --model llama2-13b --seq 1024 --iters 1000 --concurrency 8 --kernel-selector experimental --kv-cache true --batcher continuous
```
Config snippet from the job: `selector_mode=dynamic, prefer_fused=true, fallback_order=[fused,ref,naive]`
liam: Hypothesis: the refactor changed the fallback priority for long sequences, so fused kernels get chosen less often under the new heuristics -> more naive paths for some seq-shape tails. That could blow up p99 if naive has worse head latency for certain shapes.
aj: Quick triage steps:
  1) Re-run a small controlled sweep pinning selector to old behavior (selector_mode=legacy) to confirm.
  2) Reproduce on single machine with -concurrency 1 to isolate batching effects.
  3) Collect raw per-request latency histogram + kernel decisions log (which kernel chosen).
marta: Doing step 1 now. Pinned selector_mode=legacy and kicked a 200-request run on the same machine.
bench-bot: Run started (job=quick/1746204321-1, runner=gpu-42). ETA ~3m. Logs stream -> https://ci.internal/runs/1746204321-1
liam: Also get the kernel decision trace. Add `--emit-kernel-trace=/tmp/trace.json` so we can correlate latencies to kernel.
marta: trace attached in the run logs. Quick summary from the small run:
  - legacy selector p99=220ms
  - refactor selector p99=260ms
  - delta ~40ms (matches nightly direction)
  - sample size small (N=200) so will rerun with 1200 as in nightly
aj: Two immediate checks: batching behavior and kv-cache warmup. If refactor changed continuous-batcher thresholds, you might see more partial batches -> latency tail effects. Also confirm KV cache hits across requests: cold KV cache will spike p99.
marta: I grepped the trace for `kernel=naive` and `batch_size` entries. Findings: under refactor we have ~18% more `kernel=naive` choices for seq in [768,1024] and average batch_size dropped from 6.8 -> 5.1.
liam: That matches the hypothesis. Next test: run with forced `prefer_fused=true` -> see if p99 returns to baseline. If yes, it's selector priority bug. If not, maybe kernel perf regression.
marta: Scheduling a constrained 1200-run with `prefer_fused=true` and `batcher=legacy`. bench-bot job id nb-1746204321-2.
perf-bot: Reminder: include determinism check diff. Run `./tests/generate_determinism.sh --seed 42 --count 100` on both commits to ensure correctness hasn't regressed.
aj: Also run `--kernel-stats` to get per-kernel token-time breakdown; we'll want mean and tail per kernel.
sre_oncall: No infra incidents during the nightly window, gpu cluster healthy. Note: node gpu-17 had high load earlier but job pinned to gpu-42, so likely irrelevant.
marta: Plan & owners:
  - reproduce with pinned legacy selector (done) -> marta (done short run)
  - full 1200 rerun with prefer_fused and legacy batcher -> marta (job queued nb-1746204321-2)
  - determinism + correctness generation -> aj (running)
  - analyze kernel-trace + per-kernel histograms -> liam + aj once job completes
Next update in this thread after nb-1746204321-2 completes or if someone wants to run extra sweeps. :white_check_mark:
